nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2@CoSe2/CC maintains flower morphology of bunch of nanoneedles on carbon fiber with CeO2 coating layer ≈20 nm thick inducing surface roughening.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CeO2@CoSe2/CC maintains the flower morphology of bunch of nanoneedles on the carbon fiber (Figure S2b, Supporting Information). A CeO2 coating layer with ≈20 nm thickness uniformly deposits onto a CoSe2 nanoneedle and induces the surface roughening (Figure 2e-g).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals undulating nanoneedle morphology with concave convex structure in CoSe2/CC; CeO2 layer consists of ≈5 nm nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A clear observation from TEM image further reveals an undulating nanoneedle morphology with concave convex structure in CoSe2/CC (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Crystalline strips of 2.39 Å and 3.12 Å attributed to (211) plane of CoSe2 and (111) plane of CeO2 with distinct boundary.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline strips of 2.39 and 3.12 Å on CeO2@CoSe2/CC are attributed to the (211) crystal plane of CoSe2 and the (111) crystal plane of CeO2, respectively, where a distinct boundary between them exists (Figure 2h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co, Se, Ce, and O elements uniformly distributed on single CeO2@CoSe2/CC nanoneedle with Ce and O concentrated at surface, indicating core-shell structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping images (Figure 2i,j) further reveal that Co, Se, Ce, and O elements are uniformly distributed on a single CeO2@CoSe2/CC nanoneedle with Ce and O concentrated primarily at the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2@CoSe2/CC shows CoSe2 phases plus diffraction peak at 28.5° for (111) plane of fluorite CeO2; CoSe2/CC shows cubic CoSe2 peaks; CoCH/CC shows CoCH peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition of CoSe2 phases, CeO2@CoSe2/CC also exhibits a diffraction peak at 28.5°, which is aligned with the (111) plane of fluorite CeO2 (JCPDS no. 34-0394).

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2@CoSe2 shows CoSe2 F2g at 189 cm⁻¹, Ag at 670 cm⁻¹, and CeO2 F2g at 460 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra of both CoSe2 and CeO2@CoSe2 (Figure 3b) illustrate that two peaks at 189 and 670 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the F2g and Ag bands of CoSe2, respectively. An apparent Raman signal at 460 cm⁻¹ is consistent with the F2g band of CeO2 in CeO2@CoSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p in CeO2@CoSe2/CC shows Co³⁺ at 778.75/793.43 eV, Co²⁺ at 781.15/796.58 eV with negative shift of Co 2p3/2 by 0.2 eV and increased Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio vs CoSe2/CC; O 1s shows Oad/OL ratio of 1.92 indicating high oxygen vacancy concentration; Ce 3d shows coexistence of Ce³⁺ and Ce⁴⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ratios of Oad/OL in CeO2@CoSe2/CC, CeO2/CC, and CeO2 are calculated to be 1.92, 1.36, and 1.25, respectively. The Ce 3d spectra can be split into two sets of peaks corresponding to Ce³⁺ and Ce⁴⁺ (Figure 3f).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during LSV shows CoSe2 peak at 189 cm⁻¹ disappears above 1.324 V; CoOOH peak at 503 cm⁻¹ emerges at 0.924 V for CeO2@CoSe2/CC (vs 1.024 V for CoSe2/CC).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak corresponding to CoOOH at 503 cm⁻¹ emerges at 0.924 V for CeO2@CoSe2/CC and at 1.024 V for CoSe2/CC.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows weak signal at g=2.004 for CoSe2; higher intensity Ov signal for CeO2@CoSe2 than CeO2 alone.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The weak EPR signal at g value of 2.004 indicates few oxygen vacancies in CoSe2. CeO2 intrinsically displays oxygen vacancies and a higher intensity of Ov appears in CeO2@CoSe2.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2@CoSe2/CC shows Cdl of 14.94 mF cm⁻², higher than CoSe2/CC (8.68 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 6g, CeO2@CoSe2/CC delivers a higher Cdl (14.94 mF cm⁻²) than CoSe2/CC (8.68 mF cm⁻²), CoCH/CC (5.13 mF cm⁻²) and CeO2/CC (2.89 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: ks of OH⁻ adsorption at Co site is 0.271 s⁻¹ for CeO2@CoSe2/CC, higher than 0.266 s⁻¹ for CoSe2/CC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4d,e and Figure S10 (Supporting Information), the ks of CeO2@CoSe2/CC (0.271 s⁻¹) is higher than that of CoSe2/CC (0.266 s⁻¹).
